On this page

Batteries Included ​

Feluqa brings common application capabilities together so a team can focus on its Product's workflows. The direction is batteries included, but removable: capabilities should have clear contracts and be replaceable where an Application needs a different implementation.

Feluqa's ambition is to become the standard all-in-one ecosystem for building Rust applications: the breadth of reusable components associated with Symfony, the developer experience associated with Laravel, a product-building layer in the spirit of Filament, and first-class desktop experiences that belong alongside environments such as KDE. These are references for the coherence and reach Feluqa aims to offer, not claims of feature parity or affiliation.

The goal is a connected system of components, tools, and conventions that teams can adopt as a whole or compose around their needs. “All in one” does not mean every capability must be fused into one runtime: components should have clear boundaries and contracts.

Some foundations are already available. Other capabilities are incomplete or still product goals. The status beside each area describes Feluqa today; it does not promise that every battery is finished or replaceable yet.

Terms used on this page ​

TermMeaning here
Asynchronous (async)A way to express work that can pause while waiting and resume later, allowing a runtime to schedule other work in the meantime.
Asynchronous runtimeThe executor and supporting services that poll asynchronous tasks and provide facilities such as network I/O and timers.
TokioThe asynchronous runtime used by Feluqa's current server profile.
AxumThe HTTP web framework used by Feluqa's current server profile.
AdapterA boundary that connects a library or protocol to a framework, such as an Axum adapter for the Inertia server protocol.
Inertia.jsA way to build server-routed single-page applications with a frontend framework. The Rust inertia-omega project provides an alpha server implementation and Axum adapter; Feluqa has not selected it.
BatteryA capability Feluqa makes available or aims to provide through a documented contract. “Removable” is a product requirement; it does not mean every current capability can already be replaced.

The major capabilities ​

Application and runtime foundation ​

BatteryStatusIncluded capability and direction
Application foundationIn progressThe Rust developer kit (SDK), compile-time checks, and generated application metadata provide a shared foundation for Modules, permissions, resources, and routes. Application composition is still being completed.
Async server executionCurrent server foundationRust's async and .await syntax lets work pause while waiting for a database or network response. The server profile uses Tokio to execute asynchronous work and provide services such as network I/O and timers.
Web and API servicesAvailable; evolvingThe web profile uses Axum for HTTP routing and request handling, with Tower services and middleware. inertia-omega is an alpha Rust implementation of the Inertia server protocol with an Axum adapter; it is a possible future integration to evaluate, not a Feluqa dependency.

Platform and data services ​

BatteryStatusIncluded capability and direction
Identity, access control, and auditFoundations availableFeluqa Core provides account and role operations, server-side sessions, CSRF protection, tenant-bound identities, and audit persistence. The full System Control Panel, agent identities, and production multi-instance session management remain unfinished.
Data persistenceAvailable foundationsThe database service supports SQLite and PostgreSQL through SeaORM, with named pools and embedded migrations and checksums. Backup, restore, and production operations still need release-level qualification.
Panels and resourcesShared contracts; integration in progressThe panel catalogue and typed UI schemas provide foundations for registering business resources and pages. The complete System Control Panel, Feluqa UI integration, and a broad accessible component catalogue are not yet complete.
Live interactionsTyped dispatch availableFeluqa has signed, typed Live action dispatch. Browser-side state reconciliation and shared replay protection still need work; this is not yet a complete real-time synchronization system with conflict handling.

Development, extension, and operations ​

BatteryStatusIncluded capability and direction
Modules and extensibilityStatic foundation; dynamic lifecycle plannedApplications can be composed from statically compiled Rust Modules. The current lifecycle can order and start registered Modules with rollback. Dynamic installation, upgrades, and removal are product targets. Explicit contracts and extension points should let developers and authorized agents add Product-specific behavior as reviewable software.
Console and developer CLIAvailable; workflows evolvingThe CLI provides project commands, and the console framework supports named binaries, profiles, and command handlers. See Application Profiles and Starter Kits for the planned feluqa new <app> profile <profile-or-starter-kit> command shape.
Deployment and operationsProduct targetFeluqa aims to make building and operating an Application a coherent, scriptable workflow. Standalone builds outside the development checkout, production deployment, rollback, backup, and restore are not yet qualified as a complete operational path.
Agent workflowsProduct directionFeluqa is intended to support local agents and agents chosen by each organisation. The CLI should help them inspect project capabilities, propose changes, compile, validate, test, package, and distribute software through explicit, reviewable steps. The complete agent workflow and complementary agent product are not available yet.

Each area above is labelled with its current status. Feluqa's implementation continues to evolve, so the capability guides describe what is available and what remains a product direction.
